deep_analysis_units.narrative: Local input/output guardrails are rational while hazards are local and evidence is complete. A multi-agent mission changes the constraint: locally valid acts can violate squad or mission invariants, and missing telemetry can make an apparent all-clear meaningless. The reviewed design composes platform, squad and mission monitors over a durable event fabric, with monotone event identity, backend mission time and explicit unknown propagation. It buys cross-level detection and auditable provenance at the cost of evidence availability, clock/ordering contracts and a larger assurance plane; simulation and fault injection do not establish physical ISR safety. Local guardrails therefore remain the first layer, not an obsolete predecessor.

Training against one fixed inference controller is rational when serving uses the same protocol. Once production composes decomposition, critique, tool or voting controllers, controller-conditioned trajectories become part of the policy's effective input distribution. CALM samples multiple controller/module compositions and aggregates turn-level GRPO signals so the base model learns to cooperate with that protocol family. This reduces one train-serve mismatch but adds rollout variance, controller-version identity and credit-assignment cost; the reported controller/task set does not prove generalization to unseen controllers.

Request-at-a-time serving is rational when each prompt is independent. A semantic relational query instead forms an operator DAG whose intermediate prompts, dependencies and KV states outlive one request. Kalypso separates operator admission from engine-level request scheduling, estimates operator memory, pins reusable state and uses deadlock/fallback handling across stages. It gains pipeline reuse and memory-aware overlap while paying query-planner state, semantic UDF assumptions and workload-sensitive admission overhead; ordinary serving remains preferable for short independent calls.

2607.24866.title: The Missing Layer: Specification Infrastructure for AI Oversight
2607.24866.artifact: Not Disclosed — CARMA is described as a prototype instantiation without an exact immutable experiment artifact
2607.24866.delta: Versioned human-authored specifications compile into runtime policy/monitor artifacts, sidecar mediation, audit and governance interfaces.
2607.24866.source_claim: The paper supports the missing-layer architecture and prototype direction, not production efficacy, completeness or resistance to specification error.
2607.24866.analysis_old: Scattered application guardrails are workable at small scope; cross-system oversight needs one versioned specification-to-enforcement contract.
2607.24866.analysis_tradeoff: Specifications improve traceability but centralize semantic mistakes, compiler/runtime drift and organizational authority disputes.

2607.23802.title: From RLVR to RLSVR: Task Transformation Induces Self-Verifiable Rewards for Open-Ended LLM Self-Improvement
2607.23802.limitations: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.23802v1#S4 — no dedicated limitations section; proxy-game alignment and judge/human agreement bound the claim
2607.23802.delta: Open-ended tasks are transformed into information-asymmetric self-play games whose internal detection outcome supplies a self-verifiable reward.
2607.23802.source_claim: The exact v1 supports improvement on the tested transformed tasks, not that proxy-game success faithfully captures every original open-ended objective.
2607.23802.analysis_old: External judges are straightforward when labels are reliable; open-ended tasks motivate task transformation, but transformation validity becomes the new alignment contract.
2607.23802.analysis_tradeoff: Self-verification reduces judge dependence but can optimize proxy rules, exploit asymmetry or diverge from human intent.

benchmark.workload: Author-defined transformed open-ended tasks and alternating self-play

benchmark.evaluator: Game outcome plus author-reported human/judge comparisons

2607.23809.title: ACM: Agentic Context Management for Long Horizon Tasks
2607.23809.delta: The agent chooses when to compress, externalize removed content and retrieve it later, turning context truncation into an explicit lifecycle policy.
2607.23809.source_claim: The exact v1 supports the tested long-horizon policy and ablations, not universal optimality, lossless compression or correctness of every self-triggered retrieval.
2607.23809.analysis_old: Fixed truncation/summarization is rational for bounded sessions; long tasks require preserving recoverable external state and policy decisions.
2607.23809.analysis_tradeoff: Autonomy reduces fixed-window pressure but adds policy error, hidden loss, retrieval drift, provenance and storage cost.

benchmark.workload: Long-horizon agent tasks in the disclosed benchmark suite
benchmark.input_length: Long-horizon contexts; exact universal bound not disclosed
benchmark.slo: Task success/context cost; no online latency SLO

2607.23815.title: Kalypso: Relational LLM Serving
2607.23815.limitations: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.23815v1#S7 — no dedicated limitations section; claims remain bound to disclosed semantic-query workloads and runtime
2607.23815.artifact: Not Disclosed — exact v1 does not bind Kalypso to an immutable public implementation commit
2607.23815.delta: A relational query plan becomes a stage/operator DAG; the runtime performs operator-granular admission while the LLM engine retains request scheduling, with token-bound memory estimation, KV pinning and deadlock/fallback control.
2607.23815.source_claim: The exact v1 supports gains on the disclosed vLLM/Lotus/Palimpzest workloads, not arbitrary semantic UDFs, models or production SLOs.
2607.23815.analysis_old: Independent request scheduling is correct for independent prompts; relational pipelines introduce inter-operator dependencies and reusable KV state.
2607.23815.analysis_tradeoff: Cross-operator reuse and admission can improve pipeline efficiency but add query-plan state, token estimation error, pinning pressure, deadlock and workload-specific heuristics.

benchmark.workload: Relational semantic-query pipelines from Lotus and Palimpzest
benchmark.hardware: As disclosed in v1; general hardware portability not established
benchmark.batch: LLM engine batch up to 64 in disclosed setup
benchmark.slo: End-to-end query latency/throughput; no universal tail SLO

2607.23844.title: OmniCache: Multidimensional Hierarchical Feature Caching For Diffusion Models
2607.23844.artifact: Not Disclosed — cited Open-Sora is a baseline, not an immutable OmniCache artifact
2607.23844.delta: Diffusion inference caches features hierarchically across token, frame, block, layer and denoising-step dimensions using workload-specific reuse schedules.
2607.23844.source_claim: The exact v1 supports author-reported gains for SVD-XT, Latte-1 and SD3-medium on A100 40GB; it does not establish a globally optimal cache policy or cross-model portability.
2607.23844.analysis_old: No-cache recomputation is simple and exact; diffusion repetition creates multidimensional reuse opportunities unlike append-only AR KV.
2607.23844.analysis_tradeoff: Caching saves compute but consumes memory, risks stale features and requires content/model-specific heuristic schedules.

benchmark.workload: Image/video diffusion generation on UCF101, MS-COCO and disclosed prompts
benchmark.slo: Generation latency/quality, no online tail SLO

2607.23870.title: MulRobBench: A Decision-Level Benchmark for Safe and Security-Policy-Compliant Multimodal UAV Agents
2607.23870.artifact: Not Disclosed — exact v1 does not bind the benchmark to an immutable public release/commit
2607.23870.delta: An offline UAV benchmark evaluates protocol-conditioned decisions from physical observation, policy semantics and safe-action constraints, separating semantic and strict diagnostics.
2607.23870.source_claim: The exact v1 supports comparative behavior under one offline benchmark contract, not closed-loop flight safety, calibrated deployment risk or causal policy compliance.
2607.23870.analysis_old: Perception accuracy is useful when sensing is the objective; safety-critical agents require evaluating the decision under protocol and environment state.
2607.23870.analysis_tradeoff: Decision-level evaluation exposes unsafe reasoning but inherits annotation, protocol interpretation and offline-to-closed-loop gaps.

benchmark.workload: Offline multimodal UAV decision scenarios with security/safety policies
benchmark.slo: Semantic/strict decision metrics, not flight-control SLO

2607.23909.title: WorldDiT: A Unified Diffusion Architecture for World and Action Modeling
2607.23909.artifact: Not Disclosed — exact v1 does not bind the reported system to an immutable public artifact
2607.23909.delta: One diffusion transformer jointly predicts continuous action chunks and future normalized RGB patches; the future head is a training-time representation constraint and is removed at deployment.
2607.23909.source_claim: The exact v1 supports gains on disclosed LIBERO tasks, not causal/controllable environment modeling, planning through imagination or physical deployment robustness.
2607.23909.analysis_old: Action-only policies are simpler; a predictive visual target can regularize representation without turning the serving system into a simulator.
2607.23909.analysis_tradeoff: Joint prediction adds training compute and objective interference; pixel prediction may learn correlation rather than causal transition and provides no serving-time correction by itself.

benchmark.model: WorldDiT shared diffusion transformer as disclosed
benchmark.output_length: Action chunks plus future visual patches during training
benchmark.slo: Task success, not real-time control SLO
